_doc: Claims are the spine. evidence_class never collapses: T text | Tr named tradition | I inference | S our staging. state: proposed | accepted | disputed | unresolved. 'accepted' means an AI-assisted passage check has been recorded. It is NOT qualified human review and no code or copy may imply it is. Every accepted claim carries a verification record naming the method and whether a digitised text was actually consulted.

_verification_methods.none: Nothing has been checked. Claim stays proposed.
_verification_methods.ai-passage-check: An AI checked the claim against the named passage. text_consulted records whether a digitised edition was open at the time. Sufficient for 'accepted'. Never sufficient for any copy that implies human review.
_verification_methods.human: A qualified human reviewer disposed of the claim. Records their name.

claims.text: Visvamitra asks Dasaratha to give him Rama.
claims.speaker: VISVAMITRA

verification.basis: Model knowledge of Balakanda sarga 20. No digitised edition was open: this environment's egress policy blocks the hosts carrying the public-domain translation, and the GRETIL text is restricted and must not be ingested.

claims.text: Hearing the request, Dasaratha loses his senses and falls.

verification.basis: Model knowledge of Balakanda sarga 20: the king is described as losing consciousness (murcchita) on hearing the request. No digitised edition was open.

claims.text: Dasaratha states that Rama is not yet sixteen.
claims.speaker: DASARATHA
claims.attribution_note: This is Dasaratha's statement, never narrator fact. Any surface that renders this claim must carry the speaker. A caption or a line of narration that drops the speaker is a defect.

verification.basis: Model knowledge of Balakanda sarga 20, the una-sodasa-varsa line, spoken by Dasaratha. No digitised edition was open.

claims.text: Dasaratha states that he obtained Rama late, after long childlessness and great austerity.
claims.speaker: DASARATHA

verification.basis: Model knowledge of Balakanda sarga 20: the king pleads his age and the lateness of his sons. No digitised edition was open.

claims.text: Dasaratha offers his own army and himself in Rama's place.
claims.speaker: DASARATHA

verification.basis: Model knowledge of Balakanda sarga 20: the king offers the aksauhini and his own person. No digitised edition was open.

claims.text: Visvamitra names Marica and Subahu, servants of Ravana, as the rakshasas troubling the sacrifice.
claims.speaker: VISVAMITRA

verification.basis: Model knowledge of Balakanda sarga 19, where the sage names the two rakshasas and their master. Carried into M3 as the pressure the refusal answers. No digitised edition was open.
Model knowledge of Balakanda sarga 20: the refusal is explicit and is the sarga's outcome. No digitised edition was open.

claims.text: A lamp stands at the king's right hand through the refusal, and does not move.
claims.staging_note: Ours. The text specifies no lamp. Declared as a staging choice so the Ledger can show it as ours and not as the text's.

verification.basis: No source claimed. This is a declared staging choice under class S and is accepted as ours, not as text.

claims.text: The refusal is staged in a pillared court interior, post-and-lintel, on a raised plinth.
claims.inference_basis: Amaravati, 2nd-3rd c. CE, court panels: pillared hall, raised plinth, post-and-lintel construction, vedika railing motif. The inference rests on those named panels and their dated vocabulary, not on a region or an era.

verification.basis: Inference is recorded against a named visual source, not a text locator. Accepted as an inference, never as text.

claims.text: Visvamitra comes to the gate of Ayodhya and is announced.
Dasaratha receives the sage with honour and offers him whatever he asks.
claims.speaker: DASARATHA

claims.text: Vasistha counsels Dasaratha to let Rama go.
claims.speaker: VASISTHA

claims.text: Visvamitra gives Rama the vidyas Bala and Atibala.
They travel south along the Sarayu and come to a wood.
The king weeps as he refuses.
claims.tradition: Commentarial and performance tradition (Ramayana katha performance, various). Not the Valmiki spine.
claims.disposition_note: Held disputed on purpose. A named tradition is never promoted to Text. The direction may not stage weeping as if it were the text's.

claims.text: Whether Rama is present in the hall during the refusal.
claims.silence_note: The passage does not settle it. We say so rather than choosing and calling it text. The direction may show the hall without resolving the question.
